quantifier-dependent.title: Quantifier order: input-dependent witnesses succeed
quantifier-dependent.description: The explicit domain is the three integers zero, one and two. This finite example illustrates the scope difference, not a claim about every possible predicate.
quantifier-dependent.invariant: An outer existential witness must serve every universally required input; an inner existential witness may depend on the preceding input.

cmos-nand.title: CMOS NAND: parallel pull-up and series pull-down

frames.caption: Evaluate the ideal switches in a CMOS NAND gate. The parallel pull-up network conducts when either input is zero; the series pull-down path requires both inputs to be one.

conditional-strip.title: A positive strip approaches a continuous observation
conditional-strip.description: The joint density is two on the triangle zero less than X less than Y less than one.
conditional-strip.invariant: For fixed $y=1/2$, the target is $X\le y/2$ and the strip is $y\le Y\le y+\varepsilon$. Every checkpoint has positive strip mass.

frames.caption: Shrink a positive-width strip around the fixed interior observation. Its target mass and total mass both shrink, while their ratio approaches one half without dividing by a null line.

teachingPolicy.reading: Connections are electrical topology, not decorative arrows. Wire colors denote known logic levels; unknown gates remain unevaluated until their prerequisites are available.
guide: Read input polarities and fixed gate ports.
Inspect the current gate, valuation or scheduled event.
Apply the declared gate function or delay model.
Check the output, fault witness or timing restriction.

comb-falsepath.title: Reconvergence constrains sensitization
comb-falsepath.description: Toggle the primary input while evaluating only settled Boolean values.
comb-falsepath.invariant: Stable output remains zero; this model deliberately makes no physical glitch-freedom claim.

frames.caption: Stable input A=0 always gives product zero because its two branches are correlated complements. Structural connectivity does not provide independent side-input assignments or prove a stable output transition.

comb-active-low.title: Transform both sides of a polarity interface
comb-active-low.description: Observe disabled high grants and enabled low assertions without mixing input/output complements.
comb-active-low.invariant: Active-low inputs transform arguments; active-low outputs transform results.

frames.caption: Convert the active-low enable to logical enable before computing priority, then complement each observed grant. This row preserves disabled suppression and gives a low active grant only to the selected requester.
